newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto Stock Exchange to delay migrating stocks.
newsitem.headline: Toronto Stock Exchange to delay migrating stocks.

text.p: The Toronto Stock Exchange will temporarily delay the migration of 236 stocks to its computer trading system so it can run some extra checks, a spokeswoman said on Wednesday.
"What we want to do is do a double-check of the system and make sure it's fine before we go on migrating stocks," said Jane Womg, a spokeswoman for the TSE.
Womg said although it has caused them to take a more cautious approach, the delay was not a direct result of the problems excessive trading volume in Bre-X Minerals Ltd have caused the exchange.
"(But) that has prompted us to take a hard look at it," Wong said.
She said this will not stop the closure of the TSE trading floor, set to occur before the end of the month.
The computer system has collapsed twice in as many weeks due to an enormous bottleneck of volume in Bre-X shares.
Bre-X stock, which will not resume trading today because of system problems, has traded just over two hours since last Thursday either because of news-related halts or technical difficulties.
Womg added that 1,452 stocks have already migrated to the CATS system.
The stocks left on the floor include several large-capitalization shares which habitually trade heavy volumes, including Canadian bank stocks and BCE Inc, Canada's largest publicly traded company.
